classification.difficultyReason: Reframe each unknown reflex angle as a full turn minus an interior triangle angle, then combine the three relationships so the known interior-angle sum determines the total without finding individual angles.

content.prompt: What is the value of $a+b+c$? Explain your reasoning.

spec.description: Triangle with an upper apex and an approximately horizontal lower side. Reflex-angle arcs lie outside the triangle at all three vertices, labelled c° at the lower-left, b° at the apex and a° at the lower-right.
spec.mathematics: Each labelled reflex angle and its adjacent interior angle sum to 360°. The three interior angles sum to 180°.
spec.answerVisibility: Only the source givens a°, b° and c° are visible; interior-angle variables and calculations appear only in the worked answer.

answer.worked:
Let $x$, $y$ and $z$ be the interior angles adjacent to $c$, $b$ and $a$, respectively. Angles around each vertex sum to $360^{\circ}$:
$$\begin{align*}
c+x&=360^{\circ}\\
b+y&=360^{\circ}\\
a+z&=360^{\circ}\\
c+x+b+y+a+z&=1080^{\circ}.
\end{align*}$$
The angle sum of the triangle gives $x+y+z=180^{\circ}$. Hence
$$\begin{align*}
a+b+c&=1080^{\circ}-(x+y+z)\\
a+b+c&=1080^{\circ}-180^{\circ}\\
a+b+c&=900^{\circ}.
\end{align*}$$
